correctness.rationale: For iid Gaussian data, conditional on multinomial bootstrap counts, the sample-mean error and the bootstrap displacement are orthogonal Gaussian linear forms and are independent. Their variance ratio is exactly the normalized collision count. The Cauchy ratio formula gives the finite-sample coverage. Concavity yields strict undercoverage. Collision-indicator graph expansions give the exact moments needed for the Taylor remainder and coefficient. The packaged recurrence independently reproduces small exhaustive cases, moments, and numerical coverages. Risk is confined to the explicitly excluded non-Gaussian and multi-resample settings.

value.rationale: The one-resample regime is the defining extreme-computation use case of Cheap Bootstrap. An exact benchmark that proves finite-sample anti-conservatism for every Gaussian sample size, quantifies the deficit in closed form, and exposes its bootstrap-occupancy mechanism is a motivated calibration result rather than a routine restatement. It sharpens prior asymptotic and bound-only results and supplies a directly reusable diagnostic for deciding whether the one-resample limit is acceptable.
